I'm not sure I understand the question. Are you asking why the 99% confidence intervals are wider than the 95% confidence intervals? They look close in the above graphics (largely because your test length is quite long, and so measurement precision is very constant), but the 99 is definitely wider. 

Phil

parts:
That's not how confidence intervals work. Wider advertised confidence level = wider interval (assuming the method of obtaining said interval is constant). That's true everywhere in statistical inference. 

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Items fit - empirical plots - bad confidence intervals?
parts:
It's all somewhat relative, and these types of plots are really only good at evaluating the potential shape of the misfit. If you're looking for a more binary decision about fit I would rely on the numerical fit statistics reported by the package, particularly those that are known to have better Type I error control (see references in itemfit() for further detail). HTH.

Phil
